dek: LvlUp Ventures breaks down what actually gets seed startups funded now.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: LvlUp Ventures reviewed *25,000 startup applications* and says the seed-stage playbook has quietly changed.

slides.label: Who's Behind It
slides.text: The findings come from *Aaron Golbin*, co-founder of LvlUp Ventures, who has backed *1,000+ startups* worldwide.

slides.label: Money Moves
slides.text: Equity isn't the only option anymore. LvlUp financed one startup with *$1M in non-dilutive capital* almost overnight.

slides.label: Distribution First
slides.text: Winning startups build *distribution into the product* from day one instead of bolting it on after launch.

slides.label: Learning > Speed
slides.text: Moving fast isn't rare anymore. What separates winners is *closing knowledge gaps faster* than everyone else.

slides.label: Focus Wins
slides.text: About *82% of startups* still alive a year later had a strong go-to-market plan baked into their pitch.

slides.label: AI As Infrastructure
slides.text: *78% of founders* applying now use AI, but the winners design it as core architecture, not a bolted-on experiment.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: For Black, Brown and underrepresented founders raising less capital, knowing these rules can be the difference between funded and passed on.

question: Which of these seed-stage rules surprises you most?
caption_instagram:
The seed-stage playbook just changed, and most founders don't know it yet.

According to Crunchbase News, LvlUp Ventures reviewed 25,000 startup applications and found that equity alone isn't cutting it anymore. Non-dilutive capital, built-in distribution and AI as core infrastructure (not an experiment) are now separating funded startups from the rest.

The data is blunt: about 82% of startups still standing a year later had a real go-to-market plan from day one. Founders who wait to figure out distribution after launch are already behind.

For underrepresented founders raising less capital with less room for error, knowing these shifts before you pitch isn't optional, it's survival.

Which of these seed-stage rules surprises you most?

caption_linkedin:
Crunchbase News just published a breakdown from LvlUp Ventures that every early-stage founder needs to see.

After reviewing 25,000 startup applications, the firm found that the old formula (product, team, deck) no longer predicts who gets funded. Non-dilutive capital is now a real strategic lever, not a backup plan. Distribution has to be designed into the product before scale, not added after launch. And AI only works when it's treated as infrastructure, not an experiment bolted onto existing workflows.

The most telling number: 82% of startups still operating a year later had a strong go-to-market foundation in their original pitch deck.

For founders operating with less capital and less margin for error, especially in underrepresented communities, understanding these shifts before a raise isn't optional anymore.

Which of these seed-stage rules surprises you most?
